Smt. Naseemunnisa Begum vs The State Of Telangana, on 17
April, 2023
The Hon'Ble Sri Justice Mummineni Sudheer Kumar
 Writ Petition No.10355 of 2023
Order:

entities.text: Naseemunnisa Begum vs The State Of Telangana
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner, learned Government Pleader for Municipal Administration and Urban Development for respondent No.1 and learned Assistant Government Pleader for Land Acquisition appearing for respondent Nos.3 and 4.
2.

This Writ Petition is filed seeking a writ of Mandamus to declare the action of the respondents in proposing to pass an Award and to pay compensation in favour of respondent Ns.5 and 6 in respect of the subject property, as arbitrary and illegal.

3. The petitioner herein having come to know about the acquisition proposals moved by the respondents to acquire the subject property and apprehending that the respondents may pay compensation in favour of respondent Nos.5 and 6 herein, the petitioner approached this Court by filing this writ petition.
The petitioner is also claiming right, title and interest over the subject property.

4. When the matter is taken up for consideration, learned Assistant Government Pleader for Land Acquisition brought to the notice of this Court the written instructions received from respondent No.3, wherein it is stated that the acquisition proposals are at preliminary stage and a Notification under Section 11 (1) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short, 'Act 2013') is yet to be published in newspapers.

entities.text:
Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: He further stated that after issuance of preliminary notification, the respondents would strictly follow the provisions of the Act 30 of 2013 and conclude the said proceedings.
5. As the acquisition proceedings are at preliminary stage, the present Writ Petition is premature and as such this Court is not inclined to entertain this Writ Petition at this stage.
In case, if any notice is issued proposing to acquire the subject property, it is open for the petitioner to make a claim and assert her rights.

In case, if the petitioner makes any claim before the respondents, the respondent-Land Acquisition Officer shall consider the same and pass appropriate orders thereon,
in accordance law.
6. With the above observation, the Writ Petition is dismissed as premature.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Miscellaneous Petitions, if any, pending in this writ petition shall stand closed.
